title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
problem: Training and serving 671B-parameter MoE LLMs at scale exposes critical hardware bottlenecks: HBM memory capacity growing <50%/year versus >1000%/year model memory demand, FP8 Tensor Core accumulation precision limited to 13 mantissa bits (FP22) causing numerical instability in large-scale training, NVLink bandwidth halved in H800 vs H100 (400 vs 900 GB/s) constraining tensor parallelism, and all-to-all expert parallelism (EP) communication consuming up to 20 GPU SMs for control-plane operations.
motivation: DeepSeek-V3, trained on only 2,048 H800 GPUs to state-of-the-art performance, demonstrates that hardware-software co-design can dramatically reduce the cost of frontier LLM training and inference, offering concrete lessons for next-generation hardware architects about where current GPU/network designs impose avoidable constraints.
method: DeepSeek-V3 handles 671-billion-parameter training through five coordinated techniques: compressing attention cache 7-fold (516 KB to 70 KB per token) by projecting keys and values to lower rank, restricting expert routing to 4 of 8 nodes to exploit the 4:1 bandwidth difference between fast GPU-to-GPU links (NVLink) and network links (InfiniBand), and training with FP8 numbers (8-bit floating-point for speed) using tile-wise and block-wise quantization through DeepGEMM to work around accumulation precision limits (FP22). DualPipe overlaps attention and expert computation with coordinated expert dispatch via InfiniBand GPUDirect Async, while a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree topology with 8 independent InfiniBand planes per node eliminates bandwidth bottlenecks. These techniques scale to 16,384 GPUs at the same per-endpoint cost as simpler topologies, achieving 272.8 billion tokens per day at 43.7% GPU utilization with expert-parallelism bandwidth over 40 GB/s per GPU.
key_novelty: The Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network topology with 8 independent InfiniBand planes per node enables 8× scaling of 671-billion-parameter expert-based models to 16,384 GPUs while maintaining per-endpoint costs equivalent to conventional two-layer designs.
contributions: MLA: low-rank KV projection reducing KV cache 7.4x vs. LLaMA-3.1-405B (70 KB vs 516 KB per token), enabling memory-efficient inference on constrained hardware.
Node-Limited Routing: MoE expert selection constrained to max 4 of 8 nodes per token, exploiting the 4:1 NVLink/IB bandwidth ratio to reduce all-to-all IB traffic and avoid inter-node bottlenecks.

FP8 mixed-precision training framework (DeepGEMM) with fine-grained tile/block quantization achieving <0.25% accuracy loss vs BF16, with concrete hardware suggestions for FP32 accumulation registers and native group-scaling Tensor Cores.

Multi-Plane Two-Layer Fat-Tree (MPFT) network supporting 16,384 GPUs at $4.39k/endpoint (vs $7.5k/endpoint for three-layer fat-tree), with training throughput parity to single-plane MRFT (MFU 43.73% vs 43.68%) and EP bandwidth >40 GB/s per GPU.

metrics.speedup: MTP module achieves 1.8x generation TPS vs. no MTP; EP dispatch/combine >40 GB/s per GPU on MPFT; TPOT theoretical upper bound 67 tokens/s on H800 IB vs ~1200 tokens/s on GB200 NVL72
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: MFU 43.73% (non-causal) on 2048 H800 GPUs; 250 GFLOPS/token for 671B MoE vs 2448 for LLaMA-405B dense
metrics.accuracy: FP8 training relative accuracy loss <0.25% vs BF16
metrics.other: KV cache: 70 KB/token (MLA) vs 516 KB/token (LLaMA-405B GQA); training throughput 272.8B tokens/day; 2,048 H800 GPUs for full DeepSeek-V3 training

baselines: NVIDIA H800 GPU cluster (standard three-layer fat-tree / MRFT)
limitations: Hardware suggestions (FP32 accumulators, native group-scaling Tensor Cores, unified NVLink/IB NIC) are forward-looking design recommendations not yet validated in silicon; regulatory constraints capped deployment at ~2,048 GPUs, preventing full characterization of MPFT at 16K+ GPU scale.
primary_theme: Hardware-software co-design analysis of a production 671B MoE LLM system with hardware architecture recommendations
